917.t: Brother Freddie Keppard and the first instruments
917.s: Keppard names his brother Freddie, one year younger, and says he himself started on guitar while Freddie began on violin with Mr. Baboy.
917.q: He was born in... I was born in 1888. He was born in 1889. Remember the date of his birthday? On the... On the 15th of June. And I was born on February 2nd, 1889. 1888. 1888. And what was your first instrument? When did you start? The first instrument was the guitar. And when I was playing guitar,…

826.t: James Humphrey, the father, taught the family music
826.s: A speaker recalls their father James Humphrey, a music teacher who taught all the children and grandchildren, including bass.
826.ch: Arrival and the Pete Lala photograph
826.q: And James, if he wants to ask some questions, then he can get him on tape.

969.t: Father's conservatory career and Blanchin's early violin and jazz interest
969.s: His father, Paris-trained, played and conducted in New Orleans theaters; George began violin at five and was drawn to jazz despite his father's dislike.
969.q: Well that's correct. My father was a so-called legitimate musician. He studied and graduated from the Conservatory of Music in Paris, with very high honors and was considered a very fine musician. He played in the orchestras for his violinist at the old French Opera House. He conducted the…

262.t: Father as booking agent for New Orleans bands
262.s: His father booked string bands for dances near Baton Rouge, including violinist Dick Taylor.
262.q: No, he made frequent visits to New Orleans and uh, he got a lot of his ideas from New New Orleans because you know, he used to come here and uh, he, he sort of was a, even back in those days he was sort of like a booking agent for bands out of this section from around Baton Rouge, Scotlandville…

38.t: Starting violin at eight and a trip west
38.s: A full-size violin put him off at first. His mother took him to California and then Chicago for her health, and the early Creole band in California is mentioned.
38.q: Yes. I started violin when I was about eight years old, but the violin teacher made a mistake. He bought me a full-size violin, and I struggled along for a few months and got disgusted. I didn't know. I was only eight years old. I didn't know if it was the reason. It wasn't until years later that…

907.t: Birth in Louisville and musical family; self-taught
907.s: Born in 1888 in Louisville, his mother's organ and French harp started him; self-taught against his father's disapproval of jazz.
907.q: My mother's where the music came from because she played organ. And also she played, they were what they called a mouth organ. At that time they called it French organ. And she learned me as a kid to play the French organ. I used to play that mouth organ very good. My father and I. And so from that…

270.t: His father's music and early lessons
270.s: His father played guitar and viola, was in local bands, and sent Sayles to a professor.
270.q: Yeah, he played with a trio from out there in the Irish Channel. And then he went to a band called the Silver Leaf Band. And the man worked for the old Keith Copper Company, that's the way he flew to the time. We don't see you that for him.

44.t: Grandfather Bob Welch the preacher and Welch's instruments
44.s: Welch's preacher grandfather played banjo and his grandmother violin; Welch plays six-string guitar and a bit of piano.
44.q: Well, uh... He just had it around the house. Well, uh, he never... They'd go off playing on, but he just had it and had him a violin. So him and my mother, my grandmother, and we used to get together. He'd play the banjo and she'd play the violin. Then they'd change up. They'd have them old...…

843.t: Religious grandparents disapproved of his music
843.s: His father played in a brass band but not trumpet; his religious grandparents disliked music, so he played in halls and at other people's houses.
843.q: I used to leave and go play my, go in them halls in different places, go to other people's houses and go on. It didn't stop me at all. I just kept, I just continued going, you know what I mean? So, when I found myself, well, I was down here.

635.t: Musical family, the uncle's violin, Cajun dances and school
635.s: His mother's people all played music; his uncle played for Cajun dances, and he and his siblings formed string trios. Playing excused kids from school exams.
635.q: my uncle used to play a little ham fat violin, they called it, see, but all my mother's people played music. Oh yeah? See, all of them. What was the ham fat violin? Well you know, just play it around like, they used to call it the brulee. You played the dancing for the Cajuns. Now Cajuns, there's a…

484.t: Father's brass band, family music and learning to fake
484.s: His father played baritone in the Algiers brass band and held musical evenings at home; the whole family played piano. Brownlee always faked, later learning to read cornet and string bass.
484.q: i hit them loud and wrong like louie said about his vibes one time i told mark hazel he hit them loud and wrong who did your daddy play with anybody or just alone oh my father uh played cup instruments he played baritone with uh i would imagine the algiers brass band in those days they used to have…

138.t: The Brunies boys join the band
138.s: Laine's band was all young boys; the Brunies brothers joined at about eight to ten, and their violinist father trained them and played on corners.
138.q: I took them all in the band. And I'll tell you about the Brunish boys. The daddy was a good musicianer, good violin player, mighty good violin player. And he loved music. He sure loved music. That old man sure loved music. So he'd get them kids all together, he's kids, buy them old instruments and…

84.t: Getting interested in music; playing 'bass' on a chair
84.s: His father's friends held music evenings; as a boy he imitated a bass by rubbing a chair, then was bought a clarinet after years on drums.
84.q: Well, we were living back on Seals Avenue and my dad and a bunch of fellas used to get together every Thursday and they'd send to New Orleans and get a half-cag of beer. He'd buy it one Saturday and then the other fellas would buy it. They'd go around the circus like that one Saturday. And they had…

298.t: Born in New Orleans; mother's violin and early lessons
298.s: Born 1908; his mother studied classical violin and gave him hers around age ten, and he took lessons then dropped it.
298.q: The reason why I don't know, because when I was born, she had gave that up. Oh, I see. Because she gave me that violin when I got around about 10 years old. She gave it to me. Did you play anything? I took lessons from Willie, uncle's grandfather. I was going to school and taking lessons from him.…

15.t: First violin lessons at age seven; his musician father
15.s: Howard began violin lessons at seven; his father played violin, cornet and piano in Chicago night spots.
15.q: Oh, he played in night spots. When he became ill, he was working at a place called Pony Morris, 21st and Warbash.

154.t: Father the baseball player and practicing behind the scoreboard
154.s: His father wanted him to play baseball; Bert practiced between innings and his father accepted it when he joined Barnet.
154.q: He didn’t know what was going on really. He was a baseball player and he wanted me to play baseball so he was a catcher and he bought the mask and the protection and anyway, he later on became an umpire.

598.t: Musical family and playing time as a child
598.s: His father was an amateur trumpeter, instruments filled the house, and he played time on a peck horn at five; he explains his emphasis on rhythm and leaving notes out.
598.q: Yeah I would say. My older brother Pete naturally plays trumpet and is still playing. We work together quite a bit. But he started first, and my dad was not a musician per se but he was an amateur trumpet player, and there were instruments around the house all the time. Tuba, E flat peck horns, and…

214.t: Starting violin and his father's Des Moines band
214.s: Lanny began violin at six; his father played sax and led the WHO staff band, but his mother kept the horns out of the house.
214.q: I started violin when I was six years old. My dad was a saxophone player in Des Moines, Iowa. He traveled around the midwest with the band and he also had the staff band of WHO and this was when Ronald Reagan was the, Dutch Reagan was the sportscaster. My dad, who loved him immensely said he didn’t…

367.t: Father's guitar and banjo, the string family band
367.s: Young describes his father teaching his mother guitar and banjo, the uncles in a string group, and his first instrument, the zither.
367.q: Well, my father, he taught my mother how to play guitar and banjo because he was a guitar and banjo player. And there was a few bands that wanted him to come out on the road, but he wouldn‘t go out with them. I can‘t think of the name of the bands now, but they were big bands that traveled, like…

88.t: Not wanting to play: his father supplies instruments
88.s: Lee wanted sports, but in the house everybody played, and his father kept producing instruments until he learned.
88.q: And then a peculiar thing about -- you know, when you're young, you're so foolish sometimes about you know, what a child thinks, and I think the reason I ended up playing the different instruments was because I really didn't want to play, you know? No. I wasn't like Lester. I really didn't want to…

641.t: Father's love of music and the violin lessons under the bed
641.s: His father played cornet and harmonica and wanted the children to learn music; Joe listened in on his brother Frank's violin lessons from under the bed.
641.ch: Family and childhood in Baton Rouge
641.q: Yes. They called them cornets then. They didn't call none of those horns... In fact, I didn't know anything about a trumpet in those days. I think they called all of them cornets. And he fooled around with the harmonica. But he wanted all of us children to learn music. My older brother gave the…

76.t: Cousin Willie Bontemps passed off as his uncle
76.s: Marge prompts the story of his cousin Willie Bontemps, Aunt Carrie's son, called his uncle because married women could not teach school. Willie played bass, guitar and banjo and took Zutty to rehearsals.
76.q: because when you taught school, you see, my mother and my Aunt Carrie and my Uncle Willie, they were supposed to be brothers and sisters, you know.

238.t: Her father the bassist and the string instruments at home
238.s: Her father was a professional bass violin player who played all string instruments and taught her guitar, violin and mandolin.
238.q: My father was, yes. He was a marvelous musician. His basic instrument was the bass violin. However, he played all of the string instruments, and we had every type of instrument you could mention in our home in Louisiana. And I was fortunate enough to learn several of those instruments.

13.t: Born in Englewood in 1908; first violin lessons with Lewis Sanborn
13.s: Wilson gives his birth date and place and explains how an old violin led to lessons with a German teacher at age ten.
13.q: Well, it's kind of funny situation. We had an old violin sitting in the corner, and my mother figured she didn't know what to do with it, and my uncle left it there. So she figured she'd give me violin lessons, and if I did all right, why she'd keep it up. So we got ahold of a violin teacher, I…
